issues.legal_issue: Whether the circumstantial evidence was sufficient to sustain the convictions for the alleged offences.
material_facts: The convictions rested entirely on circumstantial evidence, including an alleged motive involving a sale deed, evidence that the deceased was last seen with an appellant, recovery of a body, and identification of clothing found with it.

The evidence did not satisfactorily establish that someone had impersonated the deceased to execute the sale deed; the alleged impersonator’s thumb impression was not compared by an expert with the impression on the deed, and the witness who could have corroborated the account was not questioned about the deed or the people involved.

The body was recovered more than three months after the deceased allegedly disappeared. The doctor could not determine the cause or time of death, and the panch witnesses could not identify the clothing as belonging to the deceased.

The clothing identification was unreliable: the clothes had been removed and sealed before the identifying witness saw the body, and he identified them by a paper chit and a knot. The alleged last-seen account was also not credible in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The circumstantial evidence fell short of the required standard on material particulars. The convictions and sentences were set aside, and the appellants were acquitted.
issues.legal_principle: A conviction resting entirely on circumstantial evidence cannot be sustained when that evidence falls short of the required standard on material particulars. The Court applied this principle in reviewing convictions associated with Indian Penal Code Sections 302, 364 and 201; the judgment’s introductory account also refers to Section 210. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and circumstantial_evidence_only and deed_impersonation_evidence_uncorroborated and body_identification_unreliable and last_seen_account_unreliable

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The accused appealed from convictions entered against them.
predicates.circumstantial_evidence_only: The prosecution relied entirely on circumstantial evidence to connect the accused to the alleged offences.
predicates.deed_impersonation_evidence_uncorroborat: The prosecution’s evidence that someone impersonated the deceased to execute a deed lacked expert comparison of the relevant thumb impressions and corroboration from a witness who could have addressed the deed and the people involved.
predicates.body_identification_unreliable: The body and clothing evidence did not reliably establish that the recovered body was the deceased, including because the doctor could not determine the cause or time of death and the clothing identification was defective.
predicates.last_seen_account_unreliable: The court found the account that the deceased had been taken away with an accused unreliable in light of the witnesses’ evidence and the circumstances.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction based entirely on circumstantial evidence and the deed, body-identification, and last-seen evidence is unreliable or uncorroborated, the conviction cannot stand and the accused are acquitted.
